Elon Musk is playing a long game most people don’t think about.

The idea lines up with the Kardashev scale. Not just improving life on Earth, but increasing how much energy humanity can use and control over time.

Tesla, SpaceX and Starlink all fit into that direction. Energy, transport and connectivity are the foundation layers if you’re thinking beyond a single planet.

It sounds far off, but the early pieces are already in motion.

Video

Terafab is a joint venture between Tesla, xAI and SpaceX. 

Located at Giga Texas. 
Cost: $20-25 billion. 
Target: 1 terawatt of AI compute output per year. 

For reference, total U.S. annual electricity consumption is about 0.5 terawatt.

Every step of chip production under one roof: design, lithography, fabrication, memory, packaging, testing. Currently no fab in the world does this end-to-end.

Why build it: Elon says global fab capacity covers 2% of what Tesla, SpaceX and xAI will need. Optimus robots, Tesla vehicles, AI satellites. Without Terafab, the chips don’t exist.

Three companies. One building. The compute backbone for everything Elon is building next.

FYI: Context on why Elon Musk reportedly told Greg Brockman: "By the end of this week, you and Sam will be the most hated men in America. If you insist, so it will be."

OpenAI's filing claims Elon Musk messaged Brockman two days before the trial began to gauge a settlement. When Brockman suggested both sides drop their claims, Elon Musk fired back with that line.

Now things are starting to make sense. During today's testimony, Brockman confirmed his stake in OpenAI's for-profit arm is worth $20 to $30 billion, even though he invested $0 to get it. The same OpenAI that started as a nonprofit, funded by donations including Elon Musk's $38 million.

If you step back and look at it like a normal person:
Someone donated millions to a nonprofit set up to benefit humanity. The people running it slowly turned it into a for-profit, pushed the donor out in a tricky way, and quietly built personal stakes worth tens of billions. The donor, who was always told the project was nonprofit, never got an honest answer about any of it.

That is the case Elon Musk is making in court. And every day, more pieces of it become public.




Muskonomy (@muskonomy)

BREAKING: OpenAI President Greg Brockman takes the stand, and his opening testimony reveals his stake in the company that started as a nonprofit may now be worth $20 to $30 billion.

Under questioning by Elon Musk's lawyer Steven Molo, Brockman confirmed he co-founded OpenAI in 2015 as a nonprofit and served as its chief technology officer. 

In 2019, OpenAI launched a capped-profit arm, with Brockman receiving an ownership stake.

The key exchange came when Robert K. Kry pressed him on the value of that stake.

"Your ownership interest in this for-profit is valued today at more than $20,000,000,000. Correct?"
Brockman: "Yes."

"In fact, it may be closer to $30,000,000,000. Correct?"

Brockman: "I think that may be true. Yes."

He also confirmed he invested $0 to acquire that stake. The testimony cuts to the heart of Elon Musk's lawsuit, which argues OpenAI walked away from its nonprofit roots so insiders could cash in.

Grok 4 Heavy is fast because it’s parallel.

When you ask it a hard question, it spawns multiple agents at the same time. Each one tackles the problem independently. 

Heavy then synthesizes their outputs into a single answer.

Most chatbots are single-threaded. One model, one pass, one answer.

Grok 4 Heavy is multi-threaded. The harder the question, the more parallelism kicks in. The architecture is the speed.

This is Colossus. A few things you should know about it:

Built in 122 days. Empty Electrolux factory to 100,000 NVIDIA H100s, fully operational. Industry standard for a build this size is several years.

Doubled to 200,000 GPUs by late 2025. Memory bandwidth: 194 petabytes per second.

Roadmap target: 1 million GPUs. xAI has said this publicly.

Purpose: train Grok. Every Grok response you’ve ever read came out of this Memphis facility.
